item.title: Stare Decisis: The Doctrine That Anchors Judicial Consistency
item.description: Stare decisis is the legal doctrine that courts follow established precedents to ensure consistency, predictability, and stability in judicial decision-making, while allowing for careful evolution of the law in response to changing circumstances.

item.title: Ratio Decidendi and Obiter Dicta: Decoding the Language of Judicial Decisions
item.description: Judicial decisions contain both binding and illustrative elements. Understanding the distinction between ratio decidendi and obiter dicta helps legal professionals and students interpret precedent, anticipate court reasoning, and navigate the evolution of law.

item.title: Women Rights in Islam
item.description: This article highlights the comprehensive protection of women’s rights in Islam, emphasizing dignity, respect, and justice as core Islamic values. It illustrates how Islam safeguards women’s rights in key areas such as education, family life, inheritance, and personal security. item.description: In an age where the advance of forensic science tempts the bounds of human authority, The Body as a Witness reflects upon the Lahore High Court’s judgment in Muhammad Imran alias Gochhi v. the State as a beacon of constitutional restraint. item.title: Are Fundamental Rights Absolute? A Comparative Study
item.description: Fundamental rights are often described as inviolable guarantees of individual liberty. However, constitutional practice across the world reveals a more nuanced reality. While fundamental rights hold supreme importance in democratic systems, they are not absolute in nature.
